title: An overview of Chef, Puppet and Salt

videos.script: Ansible waits for you. You run it from your laptop, it connects over SSH, and then it leaves. {{push}} Puppet, Chef and Salt were mostly built the other way round. A small agent lives on every machine. Every half hour it asks a server what the machine should look like, and puts it right. {{pull}} So when somebody edits a file by hand at ten past ten, the agent puts the file back before eleven. Nobody has to remember. And nobody can keep an emergency fix that way either. {{timeline}} In this lesson you run Puppet and Salt on the lab's laptop, with no server. You write the same small web server in both, run it twice, edit a file behind their backs, and watch each one notice. {{runs}} Chef is not in the lab, so you read a recipe instead, and see that Ruby changes the language but not the idea. {{recipe}} By the end you will be able to read all three, and know when an agent earns its place and when it does not. {{table}}
